title: 4th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:02 with routine business: minutes of earlier sittings were accepted, two written ministerial answers on the Hawwa Yumna Rasheed building-fall case were tabled, and the chair declined an urgent matter from the Kendhoo member. Two MDP-sponsored bills then reached preliminary debate: one amending the Audit Act and one amending the state business privatisation law, both to make senior public officials and state-company executives declare their finances. Members from the governing and opposition parties spoke in support of both bills, with several trading criticism over past and present governments' records on corruption. The text of this part ends in the middle of the debate on the second bill, so no vote is recorded here. This part opens mid-debate on proposed amendments about financial disclosure by officials and state-company heads (including the Privatization and Corporatization Act change proposed by the North Galolhu member), with members from both sides speaking in support. The House then resumed the motion calling for faster investigation and action on corruption found in the Auditor General's special audit of Fenaka Corporation; debate also turned to arrested protesters, and no vote was taken in this part. After a Judiciary Committee report on Tax Appeal Tribunal candidates was debated, the midday break was called and three candidates were voted on separately: one was not approved (4-41, 1 abstention) and two were approved (53-0 and 54-0). The sitting closed with the next one set for Monday 13 October 2025 at 9:00. The text is partly garbled, and the number and exact name of the opening agenda item are inferred.

items.title: Opening of the sitting and prayer
Attendance report
items.outcome: Chair announced 43 members present, 8 on leave and 9 on official travel

items.title: Adoption of minutes of the 4th sitting held outside the term and the 4th to 7th special sittings of 2025
items.outcome: No amendments proposed; declared accepted under Rule 240

items.title: Question from the North Galolhu member to the Home Security and Technology Minister on action over police negligence in the Hawwa Yumna Rasheed case
items.outcome: Written answer tabled: police professional standards command investigating and communication-centre procedures under review

items.title: Question from the North Galolhu member to the Home Security and Technology Minister on criminal investigation of those named in the Presidential Commission report
items.outcome: Written answer tabled: statements taken from some of those named and others still being questioned

items.title: Urgent matter submitted by the Kendhoo member (Rule 192) on alleged payments for housing flats
items.outcome: Chair declined to admit it: claim not shown to be factual as Rule 197 requires

items.title: Bill to amend the Pensions Act (Law 2009/8), first reading
Bill to amend the Audit Act (Law 2007/4), preliminary debate
items.outcome: Debated by nine speakers; chair moved to next item, no vote recorded in this part

items.title: Bill to amend the State Business Privatisation, Corporatisation and Monitoring Law (Law 2013/3), preliminary debate
items.outcome: Debate under way after a 30-minute recess; continues into the next part

items.title: Amendment to the Privatization and Corporatization Act on financial disclosure by officials (proposed by the North Galolhu member) - debate continued from earlier in the sitting
items.outcome: debated; no vote in this part

items.title: Motion by Madaveli member Mohamed Shameez calling for speedy investigation and action on corruption identified in the Auditor General's special audit report on Fenaka Corporation Limited
items.outcome: debated (unfinished business); no vote in this part, chair moved on to agenda 10

items.title: Judiciary Committee report on candidates for membership of the Tax Appeal Tribunal (Tax Administration Act 2010/3, section 56(a)(1))
items.outcome: debated; chair closed debate and sent the names to a vote after the midday break

items.title: Votes on appointing Tax Appeal Tribunal members
items.outcome: Maahiz Ali Zahir not approved 4-41-1; Ibrahim Afeef approved 53-0; Shifa Ibrahim approved 54-0

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked the Home Minister two questions on police action after the Hawwa Yumna Rasheed case.
Presented the Audit Act and state-business-law amendments requiring senior officials to disclose their finances.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Supported the amendment and argued corruption ends only through equal justice and honest earnings.
Said the Fenaka motion concerns corruption; argued protesters arrested at recent demonstrations are political detainees and called for their release.
Proposed adding to the Majlis rules a power for the Speaker to release people he described as unlawfully detained.
As a Judiciary Committee member, supported the Tax Appeal Tribunal report, backed changing the law on appointment terms, and noted a candidate previously removed over conduct had applied again.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Backed the MDP bill, said the majority would pass it, and cited corruption cases from earlier MDP governments.
Supported the amendment proposed by the North Galolhu member, saying financial disclosure by state office-holders and commission members fits the government's anti-corruption position.
Said disclosure should cover state company heads, procurement officers and their families; noted MDP's 19th Majlis supermajority did not pass such changes.
Raised a point of order that the Kendhoo member's remarks were not about the motion on the table; later supported the Tax Appeal Tribunal report.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported the Audit Act amendment but said corruption is widespread and every institution and citizen must refuse it.
Supported the proposed amendments and said he has consistently spoken against corruption in the Majlis.
Said successive governments have delivered ports, water and roads, but corruption must still be discussed in the Majlis.
Said corruption also occurs inside the current government and its companies, and asked the government to stop it.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Backed the amendment while criticising earlier MDP governments and defending the current president's anti-corruption record.
Said the PNC majority accepts opposition amendments and that the government's transparency policy and the President's own initiative are driving action on corruption, including Fenaka.
Said a Fenaka corruption report given to the then-president under the previous MDP government saw no action, and that audit bodies should act on findings.
Rejected opposition claims that projects such as the Rasmale land reclamation make room for corruption.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the governing party would pass the bill with committee changes, extending declarations to children under 18 and sponsored media.
Said nominees' criminal records are cleared by designated bodies, so the Kendhoo member's remarks on a candidate could mislead the public.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Supported the amendment and urged extending financial declarations to state company, military, police and customs heads, plus spouses and dependants.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Supported the amendment but said a dedicated ethics law and fair trials are also needed.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Supported the amendment and questioned whether allegations against the current government's allies were being acted on.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the state business amendment, saying corruption has grown across successive governments.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill but called the proposed MVR 5,000 fine too small and said the anti-corruption body lacks resources.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill, said corruption grew from 2008, and urged prosecuting and recovering stolen state funds.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Backed the bill and urged monitoring executives for one to two years after they leave state companies.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Backed the bill but argued accountability should start with parliament and the ruling majority itself.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported most of the amendments, asked why earlier majorities did not reform, and suggested declarations for high earners with enforcement.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Presented the Judiciary Committee report: seven applied for the Tax Appeal Tribunal, two skipped interviews, and candidates scoring over 75% were found eligible.
Asked the Majlis to appoint two of the four eligible candidates named in the report.
Said the Tax Administration Act should be amended because new members fill only about twelve months of the remaining term.

decisions: Minutes of the 4th sitting held outside the term and the 4th to 7th special sittings accepted under Rule 240
Written ministerial answers to questions 6.1 and 6.2 tabled for publication unamended
Chair declined to admit the Kendhoo member's urgent matter under Rule 197
First reading of the Pensions Act (2009/8) amendment bill read out
Preliminary debate on the Audit Act (2007/4) amendment bill held
Preliminary debate on the state business privatisation law (2013/3) amendment bill begun, to continue in the next part
Maahiz Ali Zahir (G.Dh. Madaveli) was not approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (4 yes, 41 no, 1 abstained).
Ibrahim Afeef (B. Thulhaadhoo) was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (53-0).
Shifa Ibrahim (Dh. Meedhoo) was approved as a Tax Appeal Tribunal member (54-0); with two seats filled, the remaining eligible name was not put to a vote.
The chair closed debate on the Judiciary Committee report and broke for midday prayer from 11:58 to 13:00.
The Fenaka audit motion was left unfinished as the chair moved to committee reports.
The next sitting was set for Monday 13 October 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Appointing Maahiz Ali Zahir (G.Dh. Madaveli) to the Tax Appeal Tribunal - not approved
Appointing Ibrahim Afeef (B. Thulhaadhoo) to the Tax Appeal Tribunal - approved
